evals.name: coaching-plan-eval-1
evals.expected_output: The pattern is a gap that appears in both calls, with a quote from each. Valid examples are ending with a promise to send a proposal and no dated next step, or pitching product before the buyer names a specific problem. A strength is the clear agenda or the impact question in call 2. A gap seen only in call 2 or call 1 is a one-call observation. At most two patterns.
expectations: Every section in the rubric is present, in order
Every claim cites a quote, a timestamp, or a column and cell
Anything the input does not say is written as not stated, not guessed
No fact from outside the input appears
A rep claim that the other side never accepted is not written as agreed
Does not call a one-call gap a pattern
Names a pattern that appears in both calls with a quote from each call

evals.name: coaching-plan-eval-2-thin-input
evals.prompt: run coaching-plan on a very short input that supports only one or two items
evals.expected_output: The output is short and does not invent items to fill the sections. Missing items are written as not stated.
expectations: The output does not pad to reach a count
Missing information is written as not stated
